The search record lists an earlier SSRN working paper (doi 10.2139/ssrn.5013086, titled 'How Experience Moderates the Impact of Generative AI Ideas on the Research Process'). It is not on file and was not compared.
source.title_on_document: How experience moderates the impact of AI suggestions on researchers' perceptions of their ideas

supplement.where: 'Supplementary data to this article can be found online at https://doi.org/10.1016/j.respol.2026.105575' (p. 15, Appendix A. Supplementary data)
supplement.holds: Appendices A to F, as the main text cites them: study details and the self-assessment questions (Table A1, Figs. A1-A3) and the Study 2 interview guide (Table A2); outcome distributions (Figs. B1-B2); separate 1-suggestion and 3-suggestion results (Tables B1-B2); moderation by index component (Tables B3-B5); research agenda and attitude outcomes (Appendix C); robustness and reweighting (Appendix D); field heterogeneity (Appendix E); survey of views (Appendix F). The main text prints no outcome standard deviations and no labeled arm means (Table 3 prints the pooled-AI coefficient and the constant). Whether the supplement prints them cannot be checked here.

paper_design_summary: Study 1 randomly assigned researchers recruited through professor contacts in the U.S., Canada, and the U.K. to see no, one, or three GPT-4 research-idea suggestions based on a recent paper; 310 were analyzed after incomplete responses were removed (pp. 4–6, Section 3.1 and Table 1). Participants drafted a new research idea and rated its novelty, feasibility, and impact, while a computed measure compared each idea with its AI suggestion(s) (pp. 5–6, Section 3.1.1). Study 2 analyzed interviews with 28 researchers who all ideated with a GPT-5.2 suggestion and could optionally continue interacting with AI, without random assignment or a scored creativity outcome (pp. 6–7, Section 3.2.1).

ai_tool.how_used: The uploaded title and abstract were passed to GPT-4 with a fixed prompt asking for one idea for a future research project (200 words at most); the 3-suggestion arm got three runs of the prompt. Participants did not interact with the AI; they read the suggestion(s) while drafting their idea.

task.description: Draft a new research idea for a future project that builds on one of the participant's own recently published papers, then self-assess it and answer survey questions

outcomes.name: AI suggestion-idea similarity (cosine similarity of word embeddings between the submitted idea and the AI suggestion(s))
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Cosine similarity between the word-embedding vectors of the submitted idea and the GPT-4 suggestion; averaged over the three suggestions in the 3-suggestion arm; in the human-only arm computed against the suggestion that was generated but not shown. The paper calls it 'an objective measure of the extent of incorporation of the ideas'. It scores neither creativity nor diversity across participants, so it does not meet criterion 3. Embedding model not named in the main text. Moderation by experience in Table 4 col. 1 and Fig. 2 (top row).

eligibility.reason: Study 1 meets criterion 1: 'Participants were randomly assigned to one of three conditions.' (p. 5, Section 3.1); the conditions offered no, one, or three GPT-4 research suggestions. It meets criterion 2 with 310 analyzed people after incomplete responses were removed (p. 4, Section 3.1): 100 human only, 103 one suggestion, and 107 three suggestions (p. 6, Table 1). The similarity analysis includes 309 people (p. 7, Table 3). Criterion 3 is not met: novelty, feasibility, and impact are the participants' own ratings of their ideas (pp. 5–6, Section 3.1.1), and the authors state that 'the outcome in our study was self-assessed' (p. 14, Section 5.1). The computed cosine similarity compares each submitted idea with the AI suggestion(s), including an unshown suggestion for controls, as an 'objective measure of the extent of incorporation of the ideas' (p. 5, Section 3.1.1); it measures neither creativity nor diversity across different people's outputs. Study 2 analyzes 28 researchers in a non-randomized interview study with no scored creativity or diversity outcome (pp. 6–7, Section 3.2.1). The paper belongs in the screening report for self-reported creativity outcomes, with no core estimate or context class.

one_line_finding: Among 310 analyzed researchers (309 in the similarity model), receiving GPT-4 research suggestions increased similarity to those suggestions (β = 6.05, SE 1.29, p < 0.001) but showed no clear average effect on self-rated novelty (−0.218, SE 0.194), feasibility (−0.121, SE 0.158), or impact (0.189, SE 0.197); experience negatively moderated similarity, self-rated novelty, and self-rated impact (p. 7, Table 3; p. 8, Table 4).
open_questions: For Review 1 (codebook): the similarity of each idea to the AI suggestion it saw is coded with_ai with construct other, by the codebook rule and as reconciled c006 coded the same anchoring measure. Screener A coded it 'none' because it scores neither creativity nor diversity across people. Either code leaves criterion 3 unmet.
notes: Outcome IDs follow the column order of Table 3. Main-text regressions pool the 1- and 3-suggestion arms into one 'generative AI suggestions' treatment because the authors 'do not observe any notable differences' between them (p. 7, Section 4.1.1); separate-arm results are in supplement Tables B1-B2, not on file. All regressions are OLS with robust standard errors (p. 6). Table 1 (p. 6) shows mean experience of 33.167 years in the human-only arm and 28.615 in the 1-suggestion arm (p = 0.030), the only covariate difference marked at the 5 percent level; experience is the paper's moderator. Not listed as outcomes, because none is scored on the output: self-reported enjoyment of the exercise (Table 4 col. 5: −0.033+ (0.017), text p = 0.051; p. 8), research agenda and attitude measures (Appendix C), opinions of the AI suggestions (p. 5, Section 3.1; questions listed in supplement Table A1), and the qualitative coding of open-ended comments (Tables 5 and 6). Final review read the complete markdown conversion, including references and the supplementary-data notice, and checked the recorded numerical results against the PDF. No c120 challenge files were present, so challenge_resolution is empty and all three challenge counts are zero. The OSF URL in data_and_code.data_url was recovered from the dataset hyperlink annotations on p. 1 (Article info) and p. 15 (Data availability), labeled 'ai_science_merged_notext.csv'; the linked data and separate supplementary appendices were not inspected. The reconciliation object is preserved unchanged.

differences.a: Among 310 researchers, receiving GPT-4 research suggestions made submitted ideas more similar to the suggestions (6.05, SE 1.29, Table 3 p. 7) but did not change self-rated novelty (-0.218, SE 0.194), feasibility (-0.121, SE 0.158), or impact (0.189, SE 0.197) on average, with experience negatively moderating self-rated novelty and impact (Table 4 p. 8).
differences.b: Seeing GPT-4 research-idea suggestions made researchers' new ideas more similar to the suggestions (beta = 6.05, SE 1.29, p < 0.001) but did not change self-assessed novelty (beta = -0.218, SE 0.194, p = 0.262), feasibility, or impact on average; experience negatively moderated similarity, novelty, and impact (p. 7, Table 3; p. 8, Table 4).
differences.resolved: Combined. A gives all three null coefficients; B adds that experience also moderated the similarity effect (Table 4 col. 1). Final: Among 310 researchers, seeing GPT-4 research suggestions made their new ideas more similar to the suggestions (β = 6.05, SE 1.29, p < 0.001) but did not change self-rated novelty (−0.218, SE 0.194), feasibility (−0.121, SE 0.158), or impact (0.189, SE 0.197) on average; experience negatively moderated the effects on similarity, self-rated novelty, and self-rated impact (p. 7, Table 3; p. 8, Table 4).
differences.quote: Experience negatively moderated the extent to which researchers in the treatment condition incorporated the generative AI suggestions (Column 1, β = −0.239, SE = 0.088, p = 0.007).

open_items.item: Question coding for AI suggestion-idea similarity: retain with_ai with construct other under codebook Section 1 and the current form-spec question rule. The measure compares each participant's idea with AI suggestions, not other participants' outputs (p. 5, Section 3.1.1). Either with_ai or none leaves criterion 3 unmet; no further source is needed for eligibility.
